company_description: Mid-size health platform providing teletriage and clinical knowledge search for regional hospital networks. Heavily regulated: occasional PHI, strict residency and audit requirements.
notes:
SUMMARY:
- Looking at Redwood Private (VPC) as primary path for inference to keep PHI on customer-managed network and KMS.
- Primary workload: clinical triage chat + embedding-based document search (patient records, clinical guidelines).
- Performance targets: 50-100ms tail latency for short-chat flows (<=512 tokens); sustain ~50 req/s for peak clinics; throughput for nightly batch embeddings ~200k docs.

SECURITY / COMPLIANCE NEEDS:
- Must support customer-managed KMS (FIPS 140-2) and ability to rotate keys on schedule.
- Immutable audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM and archived to S3 in US regions.
- SOC2 Type II & ISO27001 evidence required; questions around penetration testing and supply-chain attestations.
- SSO via SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
- Data residency: all inference and logs must remain in US (prefer us-east-1 primary, us-west-2 DR). CTO: "cannot send PHI outside US."

VPC ARCHITECTURE / NETWORK:
- Desired topology: private subnets for inference nodes, ALB in public subnets for controlled ingress (mutual TLS + client certs), NAT gateway for limited egress to update services.
- Inbound: only from partner API gateway IPs & their load balancer; no open internet SSH.
- Outbound: policy to restrict telemetry to customer SIEM endpoints; prefer VPC endpoints to avoid public egress.
- Need design notes on cross-region fallback (route traffic to Redwood hosted fallback if dedicated capacity exhausted) and implications for data residency.

TECHNICAL PREFERENCES / CONSTRAINTS:
- Prefer Redwood-verified open models or small fine-tuned variants; willing to test quantized 4-bit variants if quality holds.
- KV cache and prefix caching required to hit latency SLOs for conversational flows.
- HSM requirement for key attestations called out by compliance (bring-your-own-key to HSM or cloud-KMS with HSM backing).
- Want observability: token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, and auditable request traces.

RECENT TIMELINE (bulleted):
- 2026-02-18: Intro call (AE + SE) — high-level requirements captured.
- 2026-02-24: Security deep-dive with Infosec — initial checklist requested.
- 2026-03-02: Architecture workshop (Fireflies ff_20260302_7890abcd) — mapped VPC topology and discussed KMS options.
- 2026-03-05: Demo of hosted Redwood API for baseline performance; internal infra team requested private topology sketch.

POC / EVAL PLAN:
- POC: 3-week focused test in customer VPC (or customer-managed account) to validate: key management, audit log delivery, latency under KV caching, and regional residency enforcement.
- Success criteria: PHI never leaves US subnets, audit logs accessible in SIEM, sustained 50 req/s with 95th <120ms for chat.
- Milestones: week 0 design sign-off; week 1 deploy infra + KMS; week 2 run load + verify logs; week 3 final report and remediation.

QUOTES / CUSTOMER VOICE:
- CTO: "We need guarantees — not just promises — around residency and key control."
- Head of Security: "Full, immutable audit trail; if Redwood can forward logs to our SIEM and show integrity controls, we're comfortable moving forward."

NEXT STEPS / ACTIONS FOR REDWOOD:
- Deliver VPC architecture diagram with exact subnet/CIDR recommendations and egress controls (by 2026-03-12).
- Draft SOW for POC including timeline and measurement criteria.
- Prepare KMS integration runbook and evidence pack for compliance (SOC2/ISO artifacts).
- Schedule security design review with Sentinel Bridge Infosec + network on 2026-03-16.

NOTES ON BLOCKERS:
- Legal requiring PHI-specific contract language; procurement timeline potentially extends to late April.
- KMS in customer region must support required HSM profile; if not available, need remediation plan.
- Concern about hosted fallback crossing US boundaries for warm DR — needs architecture with regional-only fallback or explicit data flow guarantees.
